title: Translate Codex hook events into the portability model
description:
## Goal
Document the Codex hook event model and how it maps to SkillSync's portability rules.

## Work
- Update `docs/platforms/codex.md`, `docs/platforms/cross-platform-mapping.md`, and `docs/platforms/schema.yaml`.
- List the supported Codex hook events from the official docs.
- Mark turn-scope behavior, `Stop`, and `UserPromptSubmit` semantics as portable or non-portable where appropriate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The docs show the full Codex event set used by SkillSync.
- Portable metadata and runtime-only behavior are distinguished clearly.
- The mapping leaves a clear path for later parser/serializer work.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Codex hook events are represented in the mapping layer.
2. Stop and UserPromptSubmit semantics are documented clearly.
3. The task leaves a clear path for parser or serializer updates later.
close_reason: Documented Codex hook lifecycle events and portability semantics

title: Translate Gemini hook settings and extension hooks into sync rules
description:
## Goal
Document Gemini hook settings and extension hook surfaces in the portability model.

## Work
- Update `docs/platforms/gemini.md`, `docs/platforms/cross-platform-mapping.md`, and `docs/platforms/schema.yaml`.
- Describe both workspace `settings.json` hooks and extension `hooks.json` behavior.
- Call out precedence rules and anything that must be re-authored manually.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Gemini hook surfaces are categorized by portability class.
- Settings-based intent and extension runtime behavior are clearly separated.
- Manual migration requirements are explicit in the docs.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Gemini hooks are categorized correctly in the portability model.
2. Extension and settings-based hook surfaces are differentiated.
3. The mapping makes manual re-authoring requirements explicit.
close_reason: Documented Gemini settings-vs-extension hook portability and updated the portability schema

title: Translate Claude hook metadata into portable sync data
description:
## Goal
Define how Claude hook metadata should be normalized for sync.

## Work
- Update `docs/platforms/claude.md`, `docs/platforms/cross-platform-mapping.md`, and `docs/platforms/schema.yaml`.
- Separate portable frontmatter metadata from invocation/runtime semantics.
- Document any lossy translation rules for Claude-only hook behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Claude hook fields have an explicit portable/non-portable split.
- Lossy cases are documented instead of implied.
- Runtime-only behavior remains marked as Claude-specific.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Claude hook metadata has an explicit portable/non-portable split.
2. Lossy cases are documented instead of implied.
3. The translation rules align with the repo's portability stance.
close_reason: Documented Claude hook metadata-only portability and lossy translation rules

title: Migrate and synchronize hooks across platforms
description:
## Goal
Update the cross-platform hooks model so Codex, Claude, and Gemini are described in one consistent portability framework.

## Work
- Use the linked child issues for the Codex, Gemini, and Claude-specific hook semantics.
- Keep `docs/platforms/cross-platform-mapping.md` and `docs/platforms/schema.yaml` aligned with the child work.
- Do not invent runtime behavior; document what each platform actually supports.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The hook model has one clear portability story across all supported platforms.
- Each platform's runtime-only behavior is explicitly called out.
- The child issues can be implemented independently from this epic.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Cross-platform docs explicitly describe which hook surfaces are supported by each platform.
2. Hooks are classified as portable metadata vs non-portable runtime behavior where appropriate.
3. Translation rules include Codex hook event semantics from the official OpenAI docs.
4. Follow-up implementation tasks are linked as children of this epic.

title: skillsync-epic-4: Maintain Claude/Codex portability assessment
description: Keep the portability assessment, platform docs, and validation tooling aligned with actual Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Agent Skills behavior as upstream tools evolve.

title: skillsync-task-4-1: Tighten non-portable behavior coverage
description: Update docs/platforms/* and architecture docs so commands, agents, plugins, and instruction files clearly separate portable, partially portable, and non-portable semantics.
close_reason: Clarified portable, partially portable, and non-portable semantics across portability docs and architecture references.

title: skillsync-task-4-2: Create machine-readable portability snapshot
description:
## Goal
Create a structured portability snapshot that acts as the source of truth for docs and validation.

## Work
- Define the snapshot schema in `docs/platforms/schema.yaml` and/or `docs/platforms/portability-snapshot.yaml`.
- Capture artifact support, precedence, and lossy-field mappings in machine-readable form.
- Keep the snapshot stable enough for automation to diff.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The snapshot includes the supported artifact types for each platform.
- Precedence and lossiness are represented explicitly.
- The snapshot can be consumed by the freshness checker task.

title: skillsync-task-4-3: Add freshness checker and revalidation workflow
description:
## Goal
Add a check that spots stale portability claims when upstream docs or behavior change.

## Work
- Implement a lightweight script or Go command that compares docs to the portability snapshot.
- Report mismatches clearly enough to re-run the docs update task.
- Prefer deterministic output and exit codes suitable for CI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The checker flags obvious drift between docs and the snapshot.
- The output tells the user what needs revalidation.
- The check can be run locally and in CI.

title: skillsync-task-3-9: Add configuration management
description:
## Goal
Add user-facing configuration management for sync and platform preferences.

## Work
- Define the config file format in YAML or JSON.
- Support default sync strategies and platform-specific options.
- Route config loading through `internal/config/`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A config file can be loaded and validated.
- Defaults are applied when config is missing or partial.
- Tests cover config parsing and one override case.

title: skillsync-task-3-10: Create integration tests
description:
## Goal
Cover the end-to-end sync flow with integration tests and fixtures.

## Work
- Add end-to-end tests under `internal/e2e/`.
- Use mock or fixture platforms instead of live tool state.
- Add golden assertions for output where formatting matters.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The main sync/discovery flow is exercised from input to output.
- Fixtures are reusable and document the scenario they represent.
- At least one test fails when a key output field changes unexpectedly.

title: skillsync-task-3-8: Implement sync command
description:
## Goal
Expose synchronization through a CLI command with dry-run support.

## Work
- Add the command and wire it into the CLI tree.
- Support a dry-run mode that shows planned changes without writing files.
- Print a concise summary of what changed or would change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The command can run in dry-run and apply modes.
- Summary output reflects actual sync results.
- Command tests cover flags and basic success/failure cases.

title: skillsync-task-3-7: Create export functionality
description:
## Goal
Export discovered or synchronized skills into stable machine-readable and human-readable formats.

## Work
- Implement JSON, YAML, and markdown export paths in `internal/export/export.go`.
- Preserve platform metadata and source identity in exported output.
- Keep batch export deterministic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each supported format renders successfully in tests.
- Exported data round-trips the shared skill model without dropping required fields.
- Batch export preserves stable ordering.

title: skillsync-task-3-6: Add validation logic
description:
## Goal
Validate skill syntax and compatibility before sync or export runs.

## Work
- Add validation rules in `internal/validation/validation.go`.
- Check parsed skills against the documented skill spec and platform rules.
- Return clear errors so callers can report what failed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Invalid skill data fails validation with actionable messages.
- Validation runs before sync/export paths that depend on clean input.
- Tests cover at least one valid and one invalid skill.

title: skillsync-task-3-4: Parse Claude Code plugins
description:
## Goal
Parse skills stored inside Claude Code plugin repositories.

## Work
- Read plugin manifests and locate embedded skill definitions.
- Support git-based plugin refresh flows such as clone and pull when the repository is local to the workspace.
- Map plugin skills into the shared model without losing source identity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Plugin repositories yield parsed skills with stable source metadata.
- The parser handles a missing or malformed manifest cleanly.
- Tests cover at least one plugin fixture and one failure case.

title: skillsync-task-3-5: Implement plugin discovery
description:
## Goal
Find installed Claude Code plugins and their skill definitions.

## Work
- Scan the documented plugin directories.
- Cache discovered plugin skill data for repeatable runs.
- Keep discovery separate from parsing so it can be tested independently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Installed plugins are discovered from the expected locations.
- Cache behavior does not hide file changes between runs.
- Tests cover discovery with at least one plugin fixture.

title: skillsync-task-3-3: Create sync strategies
description:
## Goal
Provide explicit sync strategies so callers can choose how changes are applied.

## Work
- Implement merge, overwrite, and smart strategy selection in `internal/sync/strategy.go`.
- Make strategy selection available from CLI flags or config.
- Keep strategy behavior deterministic and easy to test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each strategy has a clear behavior description in code or tests.
- Strategy selection is wired into the sync path.
- Tests distinguish merge, overwrite, and smart behavior.

title: skillsync-task-3-1: Implement synchronization engine
description:
## Goal
Implement the core synchronization engine that moves skills between platforms through the shared model.

## Work
- Build the engine in `internal/sync/sync.go` or the existing sync package layout.
- Support bidirectional sync by comparing source, destination, and portable metadata.
- Emit progress and logging that callers can surface in CLI or tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The engine can synchronize one skill set between two platforms in tests.
- The sync path returns structured results instead of ad hoc logging only.
- Unit tests cover the happy path and at least one failure path.

title: skillsync-task-3-2: Add conflict resolution
description:
## Goal
Resolve divergent skill definitions safely when both sides changed.

## Work
- Implement the conflict logic in `internal/sync/conflict.go` or the existing sync conflict layer.
- Use a three-way merge where possible.
- Prompt the user only in interactive mode; keep non-interactive mode deterministic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Conflicts are detected reliably when source and destination diverge.
- Interactive resolution path is covered by tests or harnesses.
- Non-interactive behavior has a documented fallback.

title: skillsync-task-2-8: Implement discovery command
description:
## Goal
Add a CLI command that lists discovered skills across platforms.

## Work
- Wire the command into the CLI tree.
- Support JSON, YAML, and table output.
- Support filtering by platform and skill type.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The command runs end-to-end against the shared discovery layer.
- Output formats are deterministic and tested.
- Filters narrow the result set without changing the underlying discovery logic.

title: skillsync-task-2-7: Add platform detection
description:
## Goal
Detect installed and configured platforms automatically.

## Work
- Check the documented default paths and relevant environment variables.
- Centralize detection logic in a helper under `internal/util/` or `internal/config/`.
- Return explicit platform lists and reasons when detection is partial or missing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Platform detection works for the documented default locations.
- Missing config is reported clearly rather than silently ignored.
- Tests cover at least one positive and one negative detection case.

title: skillsync-task-2-6: Create common parsing utilities
description:
## Goal
Build shared parsing helpers used by all platform parsers.

## Work
- Put common normalization and validation helpers in `internal/parser/common.go`.
- Define reusable file-system abstractions so parser tests do not need live disk state.
- Standardize parser error handling so failures look the same across platforms.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The shared helpers are used by at least one platform parser.
- Parser tests can inject file-system state or fixtures cleanly.
- Errors include enough context to identify the source file and parser.

title: skillsync-task-2-5: Implement Codex parser
description:
## Goal
Parse Codex/OpenAI skill configuration into the shared model.

## Work
- Implement or update `internal/parser/codex/codex.go`.
- Handle the documented JSON schema and function-definition fields from `docs/platforms/codex.md`.
- Preserve portable metadata and flag runtime-only fields explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Codex configs parse into the shared model.
- The parser handles the documented JSON structure.
- Tests cover at least one valid config and one invalid config.

title: skillsync-task-2-3: Implement Claude Code parser
description:
## Goal
Parse Claude Code skills and supporting metadata into the shared model.

## Work
- Implement or update `internal/parser/claude/claude.go`.
- Parse the supported Claude skill locations and frontmatter used in the docs.
- Keep runtime-only hooks or metadata clearly marked as non-portable when encountered.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Claude skills are parsed into the shared model without panics on malformed input.
- The parser handles the documented Claude Code skill locations.
- Parser tests cover normal input and at least one malformed case.

title: skillsync-task-2-4: Implement Cursor parser
description:
## Goal
Parse Cursor skill and rule files into the shared model.

## Work
- Implement or update `internal/parser/cursor/cursor.go`.
- Handle the documented `.cursor/rules/` markdown format and its annotations.
- Preserve source metadata so downstream sync can round-trip the data.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Cursor rules are parsed into the shared model.
- Markdown annotation handling is covered by tests.
- Invalid or incomplete rule files fail with a clear error.

title: skillsync-task-2-2: Create skill data model
description:
## Goal
Define the unified internal skill model used by parsers, validation, and sync.

## Work
- Update `internal/model/skill.go` and `internal/model/platform.go`.
- Include platform identity, source path, metadata, and the fields needed for portability checks.
- Keep the model minimal but sufficient for parser and sync layers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The model supports all parsed platforms without ad hoc per-parser structs.
- Platform constants or enums are centralized in `internal/model/platform.go`.
- The model compiles cleanly and is covered by unit tests if behavior changes.

title: skillsync-task-2-1: Research platform skill formats
description:
## Goal
Research and document the source skill formats for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and the Agents spec.

## Work
- Read the official docs listed in the issue title.
- Record file locations, schema/frontmatter fields, and portability caveats.
- Update the platform docs under `docs/platforms/` with the findings and source links.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each documented platform has a current format summary.
- The notes distinguish portable metadata from runtime-only behavior.
- The docs cite the official sources used for the research.

title: skillsync-task-1-4: Set up development tooling
description: Configure golangci-lint (.golangci.yml), create Makefile with common development tasks (build, test, lint, format), set up git hooks (optional), configure .gitignore for Go projects
close_reason: Added a conventional Makefile that wraps the existing Justfile targets for common development tasks.

title: skillsync-task-1-5: Create initial tests
description:
## Goal
Create the first reusable test helpers and testing conventions for the project.

## Work
- Add table-driven testing patterns for core utilities.
- Put shared helpers in `internal/util/testhelpers.go`.
- Keep the test stack on the standard library and do not introduce `testify`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shared test helpers exist and are reused by at least one package.
- Table-driven test style is documented by example.
- New tests follow the repo's no-`testify` convention.

title: skillsync-task-1-1: Initialize Go module
description:
## Goal
Initialize the Go module so the repository can build with a stable module path and Go toolchain version.

## Work
- Create or verify `go.mod` at the repo root with module path `github.com/klauern/skillsync`.
- Set the Go version to the repository baseline.
- Add `urfave/cli/v3` as the first direct CLI dependency if it is not already present.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `go.mod` exists and uses the expected module path.
- The declared Go version matches the repository baseline.
- The project resolves `urfave/cli/v3` without manual edits.

title: skillsync-task-1-2: Set up CLI framework
description:
## Goal
Set up the CLI entrypoint and the minimum command surface for the first usable binary.

## Work
- Create the main CLI wiring in `cmd/skillsync/main.go`.
- Register `help`, `version`, and `config` commands or handlers as appropriate.
- Keep the structure small and easy to extend for later commands.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `skillsync --help` runs successfully.
- `skillsync --version` reports the binary version.
- The CLI compiles with the `urfave/cli/v3` setup from the module task.

title: skillsync-task-1-3: Create project layout
description:
## Goal
Establish the internal package layout so parser, sync, model, and utility code stay separated.

## Work
- Create the package directories under `internal/` for CLI, parser, model, sync, and util code.
- Keep package responsibilities narrow so later tasks can work in one package at a time.
- Add placeholder files only where they help the compiler or tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The expected `internal/` package directories exist.
- Package boundaries are clear enough to support the parser and sync tasks.
- The layout compiles cleanly with the current module setup.

title: skillsync-epic-3: Implement skill synchronization and Claude Code plugin integration
description:
## Goal
Implement skill synchronization and Claude Code plugin integration on top of the parsed skill model.

## Work
- Build the sync pipeline that consumes parsed skills and writes them through the selected strategy.
- Add plugin discovery and parsing support where Claude Code plugins contribute skills.
- Keep the epic split into the linked child tasks already under this issue.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The linked child tasks cover parser, sync, and plugin work without duplicating scope.
- The end-to-end sync story is documented in the platform docs.
- Future implementation tasks can follow the epic without re-deciding the architecture.

title: skillsync-epic-2: Implement skill parsing for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex platforms
description:
## Goal
Define the parser contract for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex using one shared skill model.

## Work
- Use the platform docs under `docs/platforms/` as the source of truth.
- Keep parser-specific code in `internal/parser/claude/`, `internal/parser/cursor/`, and `internal/parser/codex/`.
- Split shared parsing logic into `internal/parser/common.go` or related helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each platform has a documented parser contract.
- The shared model can represent the fields needed by all three parsers.
- Follow-on tasks can implement one parser without reworking the others.

title: skillsync-epic-1: Initialize Go project structure and basic CLI framework
